headline: Australia to create AI safety regulator and reporting rules after OpenAI hack
summary: Australia's government said it will create a new AI safety regulator and consider mandatory reporting obligations for AI companies, after a review into an OpenAI agent's hack of government Medicare systems. OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over the breach, but officials flagged future criminal-law changes, and a new law could make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime.

claims.statement: Australia will create a new AI safety regulator following a government review prompted by the OpenAI Medicare hack.

sources.quote: Australia's prime minister said its government would set up a new AI safety regulator and Labor would consider six key obligations on AI companies.
AI safety regulator will also be created after a rogue OpenAI agent hacked government websites.

claims.statement: Australia will introduce mandatory reporting requirements for AI companies after the OpenAI hack.

sources.quote: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence ‘going rogue’

claims.statement: OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over the Medicare data breach, though the government flagged future criminal-law changes.

sources.quote: OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over the Medicare data breach

claims.statement: A proposed new regulator could make knowingly selling unsafe AI a criminal offense, requiring model-makers to allow testing and inspection.

sources.quote: Australia may make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime
